question: Find the position vector of the midpoint of the line segment joining the points whose position vectors are $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $-4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
explanation:
Step 1: A midpoint divides a line segment internally in the ratio $1:1$.
Step 2: If the endpoint position vectors are $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, the midpoint has position vector $\frac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}}{2}$.
Step 3: Add the given vectors to obtain $-2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$.
Step 4: Dividing each component by $2$ gives $-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$.
Final Answer: The position vector of the midpoint is $-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$.
